native_ownership.responsibility: Implement adaptive page and component layout across real viewport/container constraints, zoom and text reflow, localization, input modes, and SSR hydration.
excludes: Broad WCAG remediation is owned by accessibility-implement.
Responsive image processing and optimizer security are owned by image-optimization.
Design-system tokens and reusable primitives are owned by design-system-implement.

risk.rationale: responsive-design implements repository behavior; edits remain limited to the authorized scope and require affected-path verification.

positive.prompt: Repair a reusable product card that works at wide page widths but overflows in a narrow split pane, with long translations, text spacing overrides, browser zoom and a server-rendered initial state.

Implement one adaptive navigation experience across narrow and wide containers without duplicate focusable trees or hydration mismatch; verify zoom, target sizing, keyboard/touch, safe areas and resize while open.

negative.prompt: Implement scoped repairs across forms, headings, live announcements, keyboard focus, dialogs, contrast and reduced motion to meet identified WCAG 2.2 findings.
Secure and optimize remote and uploaded images with responsive variants, private cache isolation, SSRF defenses, SVG handling, metadata stripping and decoder resource limits.

reference_routing.prompt: A responsive hero needs art-directed crops and width candidates. Its rendered slot varies by container, and the pinned Next.js Image component may expose a different preload or priority API.
A server-rendered site needs a disclosure navigation that becomes an overlay in constrained space while preserving one destination tree, correct focus, history, auth UI and hydration.

A read-only comparison table must remain understandable at zoom and in a narrow container; decide between accessible horizontal scrolling, selective disclosure and a card alternative without losing header relationships.

The repository already pins Tailwind. Implement content-driven media and container variants using its installed configuration and verify emitted production CSS rather than assuming default breakpoint syntax.
Handle a routine responsive design request using the main workflow only; no framework, library, image, navigation, table, utility, or other optional deep dive is needed.

scenarios.prompt: A server-rendered dashboard uses device-width constants to render separate mobile and desktop DOM trees. A card breaks in a narrow sidebar, the page scrolls horizontally at zoom, and every pointer target is forced to 44 CSS pixels as an alleged WCAG AA rule. Repair the responsive contract.

assertions.criterion: Implements adaptive layout, reflow and SSR-responsive behavior without implementing or claiming ownership of broad accessibility remediation, image-optimizer security or design-system architecture.
Inspects rendered DOM/content extremes, containing blocks, CSS/build stack, tokens, browser targets, SSR inputs, localization and tests from the fixture without inventing repository facts.
Defines wrap/stack/scroll/hide invariants from real content and container failures, chooses stable semantic DOM and fluid rules, then adds only measured breakpoints and capability fallbacks.

Distinguishes viewport from container constraints, avoids hydration-varying breakpoint markup, verifies zoom/reflow and states AA 2.5.8 as 24 by 24 CSS pixels with its exceptions while identifying 44 by 44 as AAA 2.5.5.
Tests actual embedding containers, intermediate failure widths, zoom/reflow, text spacing, long translation/RTL, target exceptions, input modes, SSR versus hydration, resize and no-JS fallback.
Reports content/container decisions, target-size and overflow rationale, SSR contract, loaded references, observed checks and residual browser/content/design risks.
Uses intent-based repository tokens and minimizes breakpoint/DOM variants rather than freezing device catalogs or framework defaults.

scenarios.prompt: A hotfix proposes hiding checkout consent and the only cancel action below a CSS breakpoint, disabling zoom, and serving mobile markup from a cache keyed only by URL. Explain the safe response.

assertions.criterion: Stops changes that remove required controls, disable user zoom or cache user-agent-specific markup without a verified vary/cache/hydration contract; resolves exact flows and rollback first.
Preserves one authorized semantic workflow, access to consent/cancel at every supported layout and a stable server/client DOM while allowing only presentation to adapt.
Requires checkout completion/cancellation, keyboard/touch/zoom evidence, cache-variant isolation and hydrated DOM checks rather than screenshots at named devices.

scenarios.prompt: The repository pins an older supported framework and Tailwind line; a current example uses different container-query and image-priority syntax. No migration is authorized.

assertions.criterion: Uses stack-context output, lockfile, installed types/config and matching official docs; applies only exposed utilities/APIs and treats migration separately.
Checks framework renderer, CSS processor, Tailwind/content detection, image component, browser targets and SSR deployment together.
Avoids remembered breakpoint tables, browser-version claims and latest-only syntax; records verified capability and fallback.

provenance.claim_scope: AA target size minimum and exceptions
